name: Tony Allen
hook: The drummer Fela Kuti said Afrobeat could not exist without, who left Fela in 1979 and spent the next forty years teaching the beat to musicians from Paris to London.

blurb.age13: Tony Allen was born in Lagos in 1940. He was the drummer and musical director of Fela Kuti's band Africa 70 from 1968 to 1979, and the two of them invented Afrobeat. Fela said that without Tony Allen there would be no Afrobeat. Allen left in 1979, unhappy about money and credit. In 2000 Blur sang about him in 'Music Is My Radar', and he got in touch with Damon Albarn. They made music together for the rest of his life.
blurb.adult: Born in Lagos in 1940; drummer and musical director of Fela's Africa 70 from 1968 to 1979, and co-creator of Afrobeat's drum language, which spreads independent patterns across kick, snare, hi-hat and toms so that the kit plays several rhythms at once. He left in 1979 over royalties, recognition and the band's finances. Fela's remark that there would be no Afrobeat without him is widely reported; Brian Eno has called him perhaps the greatest drummer who has ever lived. Blur's 'Music Is My Radar' (2000) name-checked him, which led to his work with Damon Albarn in The Good, the Bad & the Queen (2007). He died in Paris in 2020.
